name: patch_aob_ac
description: Cheat-Engine-style Array-of-Bytes (AOB) scan against AssaultCube (32-bit ac_client.exe). Attacker enumerates ac_client.exe's writable committed regions (heap, stack, .data, .bss, allocated buffers — dozens per game process), ReadProcessMemory each one, searches for the ASCII byte sequence `ac_desert` (the currently loaded map name that AC copies into a writable global buffer when startbotmap runs during autostart). On match, does a null-patch (writes the same bytes back) so no game state changes but the WRITEVM_REMOTE event fires. Distinct read-heavy fingerprint vs. every other technique in the corpus: dozens of cross-process READVM_REMOTE events precede a single WRITEVM_REMOTE. No allocation, no protection change, no thread manipulation. Mirrors the canonical Cheat-Engine 'scan for value → edit address' workflow but at signature-level rather than typed-value level.

extra.pattern_meaning: ASCII 'ac_desert' + null terminator — the currently loaded map name
extra.replacement: null patch (writes same bytes back — no game state change)
extra.provenance_rationale: AC's autostart-baseline.cfg calls startbotmap ac_desert on load, so the map name is guaranteed to be present in writable heap/.data buffers by the time the manipulation runs. Cross-referenced against Silme94/Assault-Cube-1.3.0.2-Offsets (2026) for AC's memory-layout conventions.
extra.expected_fingerprint: MANY cross-process READVM_REMOTE events (one per writable committed region — for AC typically 30-80 depending on thread count and heap usage), 1x WRITEVM_REMOTE (the null patch, ~10 bytes), 1x READVM_REMOTE (--verify read-back). Notably absent: 0x ALLOCVM_REMOTE, 0x PROTECTVM_REMOTE, 0x THREAD_CREATE_REMOTE, 0x SETTHREADCONTEXT. The read/write ratio (dozens of reads to one write) is the discriminator vs. every other class in the corpus.
